question: C-13 said separating direction-identity from dose needs a different design. Does pooling concept/codeword variants actually deliver one?
VERDICT: Pooling helps materially but does NOT dissolve the entanglement. d_surface's dose falls 0.840 -> 0.524 and the best ORTHOGONAL direction rises 0.114 -> 0.207 (1.8x), so a control can now carry real dose instead of scraps. But d_surface is still essentially PC1 (cos 0.9968), so the highest-dose direction remains d_surface-like and the top-dose region stays entangled.
actionable: A pooled multi-concept/multi-codeword bank is a genuinely better design for this question -- it is the cheapest available improvement and needs no new generations, only a refit over the existing three banks' cells. It is not sufficient on its own: dissolving the entanglement needs cells whose dominant variation is NOT the surface contrast.

CORRECTION_2026_08_22_audit11.actionable_withdrawn: The 'treat b=0.207 as the dose a legitimate control must reach' instruction is withdrawn. Two controls: (1) pooling three IDENTICAL copies of the bomb bank leaves dose 0.8402 and max orthogonal dose 0.1143 unchanged, so pooling per se buys nothing -- all the gain comes from the three banks' d_surface being non-collinear (cos 0.607/0.662/0.170); (2) the direction carrying the new 0.207 dose is ITSELF a surface contrast (cos 0.66 with knife's d_surface, 0.61-0.63 with button's), and removing every bank's own d_surface from its own cells leaves 0.1614 of pooled spread against the single bank's 0.1598 -- pooling adds NO non-surface variance.
CORRECTION_2026_08_22_audit11.corrected_reading: Pooling three codewords whose surface directions sit 50-80 degrees apart lets a bomb-orthogonal control carry OTHER codewords' surface dose. It does not move the design toward cells whose dominant variation is not the surface contrast, which was the stated goal.
CORRECTION_2026_08_22_audit11.arithmetic_unaffected: All eight published numbers reproduce to 4 decimals; the error is in the actionable drawn from them, not the computation.
CORRECTION_2026_08_22_audit11.frontier_note: The forced-|cos| row assumes a vanishing cross term; the true Pareto frontier gives ~0.63 single / ~0.38 pooled, so the published figures overstate the forced collinearity.
